polities.name: Kingdom of Aristonicus (Eumenes III)
polities.summary: Pretender state of Aristonicus, who resisted Rome's inheritance of the Attalid kingdom with support from slaves and the rural poor (the Heliopolitai).

polities.name: Italia (Italian insurgent confederation)
polities.summary: State formed by the insurgent Italian allies in the Social War, capital Corfinium (renamed Italia), with a senate, two consuls and twelve praetors; Samnite and Lucanian resistance continued into 82.

polities.name: Sullan forces
polities.summary: Armies and adherents of Sulla in the civil wars of 88-87 and 83-81.

polities.name: Marian-Cinnan regime
polities.summary: Faction of Marius, Cinna and Carbo, which controlled Rome 87-82.

polities.name: Lepidan insurgents
polities.summary: Forces of the consul Lepidus in his revolt against the Sullan settlement.

polities.name: Sertorian Spain
polities.summary: Romano-Iberian state of the Marian exile Quintus Sertorius, with a counter-senate at Osca.

polities.name: Spartacus' slave army
polities.summary: The army of escaped gladiators and slaves led by Spartacus in Italy.

polities.name: Catilinarian insurgents
polities.summary: Catiline's conspirators and Manlius' army in Etruria.

polities.name: Caesarians
polities.summary: Julius Caesar's forces in the civil war of 49-45.

polities.name: Pompeians
polities.summary: The senatorial forces led by Pompey in 49-48 and their continuation under Metellus Scipio, Cato, Pompey's sons and Sextus Pompey to 36.

polities.name: Liberators (Brutus and Cassius)
polities.summary: The forces of Caesar's assassins, which held the eastern provinces in 43-42.

polities.name: Triumvirs (Second Triumvirate)
polities.summary: The legal college of Antony, Lepidus and Octavian under the lex Titia, and their armies.

polities.name: Antonians
polities.summary: Forces of Mark Antony and his brother Lucius in their wars against the senate (44-43), Octavian at Perusia (41-40) and at Actium (31-30).

polities.name: Mytilene
polities.summary: Chief city of Lesbos, which handed Manius Aquillius to Mithridates and held out against Rome until 80/79.

polities.name: Remi
polities.summary: Belgic people around Durocortorum (Reims), Caesar's loyal allies from 57.

polities.name: Nervii
polities.summary: The most warlike Belgic people, nearly destroyed by Caesar at the Sabis (57).

polities.name: Atuatuci
polities.summary: Belgic people said to descend from Cimbri and Teutones left behind in 102; enslaved by Caesar in 57.

polities.name: Veneti (of Armorica)
polities.summary: Seafaring people of southern Brittany, defeated at sea by Decimus Brutus in 56.

polities.name: Eburones
polities.summary: Belgic-Germanic people under Ambiorix who destroyed a Roman force at Atuatuca (54); extirpated by Caesar in 53.

polities.name: Seduni and Veragri
polities.summary: Alpine peoples of the upper Rhône (Valais) who attacked Galba at Octodurus (57).

polities.name: Carnutes
polities.summary: Gallic people around Cenabum, seat of the annual druidic assembly, who began the revolt of 52.

polities.name: Bituriges Cubi
polities.summary: Gallic people whose capital Avaricum (Bourges) Caesar stormed in 52.

polities.name: Cadurci
polities.summary: Gallic people of the Lot valley; last resistance at Uxellodunum (51).

polities.name: Iapydes
polities.summary: Illyrian-Celtic people of the Lika region whose capital Metulum Octavian besieged in 35.
